name: Ethbaal
title: King of the Sidonians and Jezebel's father
summary: Ethbaal (also known as Ithobaal) was king of the Sidonians (Phoenicia) and father of Jezebel, who became queen in Israel through her marriage to King Ahab. He is known for his role in promoting Baal worship in Israel through his daughter's influence. According to the ancient historian Josephus, he was also a priest of Baal who seized power through a coup.

keyEvents.title: Ethbaal mentioned as Jezebel's father
keyEvents.description: Ethbaal is introduced in the Bible as king of the Sidonians and father of Jezebel, who married King Ahab of Israel.

keyEvents.title: Ahab's marriage to Jezebel
keyEvents.description: King Ahab of Israel married Jezebel, daughter of Ethbaal, king of the Sidonians, which led to widespread idolatry in Israel.

keyEvents.title: The spread of Baal worship in Israel
keyEvents.description: As a result of the alliance between Ahab and the house of Ethbaal, a temple for Baal was built in Samaria, and the cult of Baal received official support in the kingdom of Israel.

keyEvents.title: Jezebel's persecution of the Lord's prophets
keyEvents.description: Jezebel, daughter of Ethbaal, persecuted and killed the Lord's prophets in Israel, demonstrating the destructive influence of the Phoenician royal house.

keyEvents.title: Elijah's confrontation with the prophets of Ba'al
keyEvents.description: The prophet Elijah challenged the 450 prophets of Ba'al and 400 prophets of Asherah who were supported by Jezebel in a dramatic confrontation on Mount Carmel, which was a direct result of Ethbaal's religious influence.
